notes.note: Introduction of the DHCP step.

segment.source: Tenko can hand out addresses on one network right away. Describe the first scope here; it is created when setup finishes, and more scopes are added on the DHCP pages.

notes.note: Safety note of the DHCP step: only one DHCP server may answer on a network.

segment.source: Switch off any other DHCP server on the same network first (the router's, an old server's): two servers handing out addresses on one network give clients conflicting answers.

segment.source: Under Hardened a new scope serves only clients on the allow list of the MAC filters. Add the clients' MAC addresses on the DHCP pages.

notes.note: Choice: requests are relayed by the gateway (relay mode).

segment.source: Relayed by the gateway

notes.note: Description of relay mode.

segment.source: The gateway relays the requests of each network to this server's address (a DHCP relay or helper address). Works in a container and on Windows; recommended.

notes.note: Choice: the server answers clients on its own network directly (direct mode).

segment.source: Directly on an interface

notes.note: Description of direct mode.

segment.source: This server answers the broadcasts of the network its interface is on. On Linux it needs the CAP_NET_RAW capability.

segment.source: Tenko keeps each client's MAC address, host name and the options it sends with its leases, and the lease history for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} under this profile.

segment.source: Enter the network as an IPv4 prefix such as 192.0.2.0/24 (length 8 to 30).

segment.source: The pool must start before it ends.

notes.note: Why the DHCP step cannot be left: the DNS servers are wrong.

segment.source: Enter one to eight IPv4 addresses of DNS servers, or this server's address.

notes.note: Why the DHCP step cannot be left: the lease time is wrong.

segment.source: The lease time is a whole number of hours or days, from one hour to one year.
